entries.proposition: Direction opposite to the Cntnap2 null: in adult glutathione-deficient (Gclm knockout) mice the reticular-nucleus neurons have lower T-type current density, weaker rebound bursting and a more negative potential needed for burst firing; the proportion of neurons bursting at rest was 25 percent (3 of 12) versus 71 percent in wild type (Fisher p = 0.02).
entries.snippet: We found a lower proportion of neurons displaying bursting behavior at resting membrane potential (RMP) in KO (25.0%, 3/12) compared to WT mice (71.4%, 10/13, Fisher exact test, p = 0.02)
entries.anchor: Results, Altered bursting profile of TRN neurons in adult Gclm-KO mice

entries.proposition: Age dependence within one model: the T-type and SK current densities of knockout reticular neurons did not differ from wild type at postnatal days 20 to 30, and hypofunction emerged in adulthood (days 60 to 75); an additional early-life oxidative challenge (days 10 to 20) precipitated the hypofunction in peripubertal knockout mice and in wild-type mice with transient glutathione deficit; an antioxidant treatment prevented it.
entries.snippet: Thus, hypofunction of T-Ca2+ channels in TRN of Gclm-KO mice emerges later during late adolescence/early adulthood.
entries.anchor: Results, Normal T-Ca2+ and SK currents in peripubertal Gclm-KO mice

entries.proposition: A redox mechanism the authors propose: Cav3.2 current is redox sensitive (oxidising agents decrease and reducing agents increase it) and reduced Cav3.3 expression was found in adult knockout reticular nucleus; the hypofunction is attributed to oxidative stress, with the authors noting the mechanism warrants further investigation.
entries.snippet: Thus, oxidizing and reducing molecules respectively decrease and enhance CaV3.2-dependent currents in TRN neurons [51].

entries.proposition: Two different non-channel lesions move the same neurons' T-type current in opposite directions (Cntnap2 null: increased, section 8; glutathione deficiency and the MAM model: decreased), and a decrease can be age-gated. Direction cannot be inferred from the fact that a non-channel gene is lost.
entries.snippet: The finding that OxS is accompanied with a decrease of T-Ca2+ currents in TRN neurons of MAM mice, similarly to GBR-treated Gclm-KO mice, further supports that OxS causes hypofunction of T-Ca2+ channels.
entries.anchor: Results, OxS reduced T-Ca2+ and SK current densities in TRN neurons of MAM mice
